question.text: A mass $\mathrm{m}$ hangs with the help of a string wrapped around a pulley on a frictionless bearing. The pulley has mass $\mathrm{m}$ and radius $\mathrm{R}$. Assuming pulley to be a perfect uniform circular disc, the acceleration of the mass $m$, if the string does not slip on the pulley, is

solution.text: $$ \begin{aligned} & M g-T=M a \quad \quad \ldots \ldots (1)\\ & T \times R=I \alpha=\frac{1}{2} M^2 \alpha \\ & T=\frac{1}{2} M a \quad(a=\alpha R) \quad \quad \ldots \ldots (2) \end{aligned} $$ From (1) and (2) $a=\frac{2 g}{3}$
